prompt:
Write 9 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1111; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Nothing independent confirms the accident: no witnesses, no photos and no other report.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured driver reported being struck while turning left at an intersection. The claimant, who has no legal representative, gave a brief account during the first call.

Entry 2: The insured driver is listed on the policy, and nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 3: The police report places the claimant in the other vehicle at the scene. No witnesses to the collision itself have come forward, and no photographs or second report have been submitted.

Entry 4: The damage to the claimant's vehicle lines up with the impact described, and no earlier damage to that vehicle appears in the records.

Entry 5: The claimant reports neck strain and was seen at a clinic shortly after the collision. The reported injury is plausible for a crash of this type.

Entry 6: The claimant has told the same account in every conversation so far, including the order of the turn and where the vehicles made contact.

Entry 7: Medical records show no earlier injury to the neck or upper back. Treatment has followed a usual course, with visits tapering as symptoms eased.

Entry 8: Apart from the police record placing the claimant at the scene, no independent source has been located that confirms how the accident happened.

Entry 9: Treatment has continued to taper as the claimant improves. The file remains open pending a final medical update before the injury component is closed.
